name: ACLED fine-grained event classification corpus
description: We introduce a new set of benchmark datasets derived from ACLED data for fine-grained event classification and compare the performance of various state-of-the-art models on these datasets, including SVM based on TF-IDF character n-grams and neural context-free embeddings (GLOVE and FASTTEXT) as well as deep learning-based BERT with its contextual embeddings. The best results in terms of micro (94.3-94.9{\%}) and macro F1 (86.0-88.9{\%}) were obtained using BERT transformer, with simpler TF-IDF character n-gram based SVM being an interesting alternative. Further, we discuss the pros and cons of the considered benchmark models in terms of their robustness and the dependence of the classification performance on the size of training data.
reputation: Used in event classification and political/social conflict NLP research; BERT-based models are commonly reported baselines.
notes: Dataset exhibits class imbalance and domain specificity (political/conflict events); performance sensitive to training data size; common baseline is BERT—this is a non-LLM-specific classification benchmark.
